title: How do you guys make sure your agent doesn't waste resources?
author: Pretend_Success_6947
selftext:
I have been going through some of the thinking my agent has been doing when weighing different investments and it's very redundant. It constantly opts for searching either through its memory system or the internet for things that it did many times before. I feel like the main bottleneck is just compiling everything the agent needs into its memory with as few tool calls as possible because these really do bloat away its attention.

I was wondering what you guys do to combat this? Do you just aggressively cache, or do you try to give it some kind of pre-compiled state? Thanks in advance.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: precompiled state. a plain script builds a morning brief before the agent starts (prices, positions, what it concluded yesterday and when), and tool calls only go to what changed since. most of the re-searching is an agent not trusting a memory with no date on it. a dated verdict per idea is the core of Quantradin, an app I made where a connected agent tests a rule once on past prices and the result stays on file. quantradin.com. what does yours re-search most, prices or news?

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
Not an agent exactly, but with my LLM features I stopped letting the model go fetch things on its own. I build a small summary before the call (latest candles, a few indicators, what changed since the last run) and pass it in. Way fewer tool calls, and it stops looking up stuff it already "knows".

Caching helped less than I expected tbh, because the model still decides to search again anyway.
